Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orchard's engineering and ML teams are excited about the throughput numbers and the latency consistency we saw in the dedicated pool. Before procurement will sign, they want a short addendum that covers two items we couldn't fully resolve in the SOW:

1) Explicit uptime / reserved GPU commitment for our production pool (we need a clear definition of reserved GPUs vs. usable-by-other-tenants during peak).
2) Queueing / preemption behavior during nightly batch jobs — we run a heavy ETL between 02:00–04:00 PT and need to understand how that will affect in-flight real-time requests and if we can request a carve-out.

Can you share a short proposal (1–2 pages) that we can attach to the purchase order? Procurement also asked for an example of the credit calculation if Redwood misses the throughput SLA.

Sanjay (cc) will be handling the legal/procurement coordination.

Thanks,
Ari

Ari — appreciate the clear ask. Attached is an initial draft (draft_sla_addendum_v1.docx) that attempts to do two things: define reserved GPUs in a way that matches your usage pattern, and propose queueing/fallback behavior during the 02:00–04:00 nightly window. High-level summary:

- Reserved capacity: we will reserve N physical GPU units mapped to your tenant (you pay reserved-node charges). During normal operations these GPUs are dedicated to your workloads; during extreme system-wide pressure (rare, described in force-majeure section) we may enable preemption but only after defined escalation and with replacement capacity within a defined window.
- Nightly ETL window: we propose a soft carve-out option where you can opt-in to a nightly priority lane for real-time traffic (we hold a small concurrency buffer during 02:00–04:00). This is priced as an add-on and configurable per month.
- Throughput SLA & credits: example credit formula included (percentage of monthly reserved tokens / p99 tail breach buckets).

Ben (cc) can confirm the technical feasibility and whether we can guarantee replacement capacity within the 90-minute window in the doc. Laura, can you confirm the customer success /finance view on the credit calculation?

I'll also attach the example SOW PDF we usually provide. If this looks good I can turn the doc redline-ready for your legal.

Ari — quick technical notes to make the draft actionable:

- "Reserved GPUs" = physical GPU slots in your dedicated pool. We map instances to your tenant with exclusive allocation. That means your KV cache and model weights stay resident and unaffected by multi-tenant binpacking.
- Preemption policy: our runtime does allow preemption of best-effort tasks; however, for reserved GPUs we can set a strict preemption window. For the proposed 02:00–04:00 carve-out we can guarantee a concurrency buffer (e.g., 10% of your baseline qps) held for real-time requests. If your nightly batch needs extra spiky capacity we can route that to a preemptible burst pool with automatic eviction once real-time load rises.
- Replacement capacity SLA: committing to a hard physical replacement (e.g., adding a node within X minutes) requires reserved buffer slots in our capacity plan. We can offer a 90-minute replacement SLA for one off physical node failures if you purchase the resilience add-on.

Risk/Tradeoffs: holding buffer headroom increases cost. Our suggested approach in the attachment balances cost vs. tail latency guarantees — happy to adjust the numbers based on your billing tolerance.

Jonas — if you have runbook language for outage escalation and the credit calc, can you drop a short paragraph we can insert?

-ben

Thanks Ben — this is the direction we were hoping for. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

- They want the credit calculation to be deterministic and tied to a simple observable (monthly % of reserved GPU-hours not met and tail-latency p99 misses). The example formula you provided is OK but procurement insists on a worked example with numbers for our PO.
- For replacement capacity: 90 minutes is reasonable, but we need the runbook steps listed (who we call, escalation path, Slack/phone contact) so procurement can sign off.
- Can you also note whether the nightly buffer is configurable per week vs. per month? Some of our teams plan ad-hoc heavy batches and would prefer weekly toggles.

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet procurement uses to evaluate credit language — procurement_requirements.xlsx. If you can return a doc with the worked example and runbook language by end of day Friday our procurement team will try to get the PO processed next week.

Ari

Ari — thanks, we've incorporated procurement's asks into an updated addendum. Summary of changes included in the attached version and inline below: 

- Deterministic credit example: added a worked example using your N=8 reserved GPUs, with credit tiers based on percentage of monthly reserved GPU-hours missed and p99 latency windows. Example: if reserved GPU-hours fall short by 4% in a month and p99 tail exceeds the committed threshold for >2% of requests, the credit equals 5% of monthly reserved fee (worked numbers included).
- Runbook & escalation: added contact ladder (Level 1 on-call -> Solutions lead -> Ops manager) with Slack escalation channel, phone numbers and an SLA timeline (ack within 15min, mitigation comms in 45min, replacement within 90min when resilience add-on purchased).
- Nightly buffer toggles: made the buffer configurable weekly via the Console API (toggle request takes effect within 4 hours) and monthly for billing cycles. We note the API endpoint and a sample cURL in the appendix.

Next steps:
1) I've uploaded the redline-ready addendum to DocuSign for signature: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-orchard-sla
2) If procurement wants a short phone walk-through of the runbook and credit calc, Ben and Jonas are available Mon/Tue next week.
3) Once signed we'll schedule a 30-min kickoff to wire the reserve pool and enable the weekly buffer toggle for a 2-week evaluation.

Attachment: orchard_health_capacity_sow.pdf (SOW with revised addendum embedded)

Let me know if you want any final edits. Appreciate the quick collaboration — looking forward to getting Orchard live on dedicated.

Best,
Marissa
